texts: good. the Council, the deciding and the feather rations all come through as one plain habitual fact.
good. parses as a habitual hearing with the Council and the progress reports both covered.
good. same clean shape as the apprentice-report sentence, with the compound kept whole and still recorded as a kind of report.
good. the "when" clause becomes a fireable rule: any Keeper's retirement triggers the Council re-staffing that Keeper's station, and the station stays tied to that Keeper.

bad: "re-staffs" was reduced to plain "staff" plus a repetition tag, a carrier the instruction set only allows for the free word "again", so the "re-" part of the meaning ends up somewhere it cannot legally sit; the rule also keys the re-staffing to the Keeper rather than to the death that triggers it. Write the repetition as its own word: "When a Keeper dies, the Council staffs that Keeper's station again."

mixed: the reading-aloud, the Council and the letters' origin all come through, but "other" is asserted of the set of villages as a whole rather than of each village, and as a bare contrast word ("other than ours") it has no licensed encoding at all, so that restriction is either mis-stated or lost. Replace it with a property each village actually has: "The Council reads letters from neighbouring villages aloud." If the point is specifically villages other than your own, name your own village rather than relying on "other".
